### Row 1 — chunk-planner v18 §3 cascade-discipline: CheckContext-build cost estimation for handler-refactor cascades

**Target:** `/root/projects/phi/.claude/agents/chunk-planner.md` §3 "cascade-artifact discipline" (extend).

**Diff intent:**
```diff
 ### §3 cascade-artifact discipline (CH-13 retro Row 2 / v3+)

 For each cascade-grep target, predict aggregate edit sites + classify
 production vs test. Pause threshold: actual sites > 1.5× upper bound.

+### Handler-refactor cascade cost addendum (CH-26 retro Row 1, cycle hex `d1cb9e1f`)
+
+When the chunk refactors ≥ 2 handlers to invoke `check_permission` (or any
+other Permission-Check engine entry point) from a bespoke-gated baseline,
+enumerate each handler's **CheckContext-build cost** at plan-time:
+
+- `Manifest` construction (ResourceRef + Action + Subject wiring): ~0.5-1 ed per handler.
+- Bespoke-gate threading (preserving the existing gate as defence-in-depth or
+  routing the engine's verdict to the bespoke surface): ~0.5-1 ed per handler.
+- Metric injection (e.g., `NoopMetrics` or `default()` parameter): ~0.1-0.2 ed per handler.
+- Acceptance-suite blast-radius (per-handler test rebuild): ~0.3-0.5 ed per handler.
+
+Default per-handler CheckContext-build cost estimate: **~1.5-2 ed per handler**.
+Plan §7 phase scoping must absorb this. If the WIDE-handler-refactor scope
+spans ≥ 7 handlers, the cycle SHOULD be split (e.g., ship advisory-only
+invocations in cycle N + blocking-gate tightening in cycle N+1) BEFORE
+plan-locking, NOT discovered mid-cycle.
```

**Rationale:** CH-26 F1.b WIDE planner v2 estimate was ~5 ed across ≥ 7 handlers; actual was ~12-15 ed. The CheckContext-build cost per handler (~1.5-2 ed) compounded over 7 handlers to ~10-14 ed, exceeding the v2 estimate by 2-3×. Implementer surfaced at Partial-P2; user-routed to advisory-only F1.b + CH-27 carve-out. Precedent: **CH-25 introduced the synth-owner-grant engine path that CH-26 attempted to consume across 7 handlers**; the CheckContext-build cost was not yet known at CH-25 plan-time.

**Why:** the planner's cascade-discipline framework currently covers struct/enum cardinality cascades + fixture sites but does NOT extend to handler-refactor cascades where each refactor site carries a hidden CheckContext-build cost. Adding this estimation framework upfront prevents mid-cycle scope-revisions (CH-26's hybrid Option-A routing) by surfacing the underestimate at gate-1.

**How to apply:** edit `chunk-planner.md` §3 section; bump version v17 → v18; log in `_changelog.md`. Closes audit-cycle gap §3 row "cycle-audit §6.3 row 1".

**Precedent priors:** CH-13 retro Row 2 cascade-discipline (chunk-planner v3); CH-23/24 cascade-grep widening for multi-site phi-core-type-shared types (planner v9 R7); CH-25 Row 4 canonical-script-reuse strengthening (canonical-script-extension discipline). This row continues the cascade-discipline framework.

```diff
+- **Session-interrupt mid-audit kill (NEW CH-26 retro Row 5, cycle hex `d1cb9e1f`)**:
+    if the expected audit log file (`audit-<letter>-iter<N>.md`) does NOT
+    appear within reasonable time post-spawn (suggested: 30-60 minutes for
+    a normal audit; longer if the audit involves cargo test/clippy), suspect
+    session-interrupt mid-flight killed the sub-agent. Re-dispatch with the
+    SAME prompt is safe (the sub-agent is stateless across spawns; no
+    partial-file-state corruption risk for the resumed run). The re-dispatch
+    is NOT counted as an audit-fix-loop iteration (the iteration counter
+    advances only on FAIL/PARTIAL → tactical/architectural re-spawn).
```

**Rationale:** CH-26 Audit-A was re-dispatched once after a session-interrupt killed the original run mid-flight. The orchestrator detected via absence of expected audit log file post-spawn; re-dispatch worked cleanly. NEW pattern; codifying the detection + safe-re-dispatch policy in CLAUDE.md ensures future cycles handle the same scenario consistently.

**Why:** sub-agent dispatches are stateless across spawns (no on-disk partial-file-state to corrupt; the audit log file is written atomically at audit completion). A session-interrupt mid-flight that kills the sub-agent simply means no output appears. Codifying the policy as "re-dispatch is safe + not counted as iteration" prevents future orchestrators from misattributing the re-dispatch to a workflow gap.

**How to apply:** edit `/root/projects/phi/CLAUDE.md` §"Audit-fix loop" + `/root/projects/phi/baby-phi/CLAUDE.md` §"Audit-fix loop" (both files share the section; keep synchronized). Closes audit-cycle gap §3 row "Session-interrupt resilience".

**Precedent priors:** CLAUDE.md Audit-fix loop section has been extended multiple times (Trivial-1L/Trivial-multi sub-tiers at CH-14, Iteration cap at CH-13, gate-2 doc-sync widened sweep at CH-15). This row adds a session-interrupt resilience clause.
